Ellen —

Thanks again for the constructive conversation earlier. As discussed, attached is our proposed Exhibit (Redwood_Exhibit_Pricing_v2.docx) with two items we wanted to call out specifically for ACME legal and procurement:

1) Annualization vs monthly true-up: we propose an annual true-up mechanic (standard for our enterprise orders) rather than a month-by-month floor enforcement. That lets ACME smooth seasonality while preserving overall minimum revenue.

2) Floor split across product bands: we suggested splitting the committed floor into Base and Burst bands (30/70 example in the table) so you only pay the high floor rate on sustained baseline usage.

Practical asks from our side: can you confirm whether ACME legal will accept annual true-up with an interim monthly stabilization mechanism (e.g., temporary credits that are reconciled at the annual true-up)? Also, would ACME be open to a per-product SKU floor for the Base band (rather than a single aggregated floor) for the enterprise SKUs you called out?

Attached: Redwood_Exhibit_Pricing_v2.docx (exhibit with example calculations and sample clause language).

Happy to jump on a quick call if it helps — propose tomorrow 11am PT if that works.

Thanks,
Karthik

Karthik —

Thanks for the exhibit. ACME legal pushed back on the annualization language in Exhibit B, Section 3(c). They redlined and asked us to preserve a monthly minimum obligation to avoid cash-flow unpredictability across product lines.

They also asked for an explicit worked example showing a 12-month annualization vs monthly floor so they can see worst-case exposure. Finally, one of our in-house architects asked whether the floor could be applied per-SKU rather than as a single aggregate floor across all units — their preference is per-SKU, but procurement is sensitive to administration overhead.

I've attached our redline: Acme_Redline_OrderForm.pdf (highlights on Sec 3(c), Exhibit B tables).

We can take the annualization concept, but ACME legal wants either: (a) a hard monthly floor (not ideal for us), or (b) a hybrid where there is a soft monthly stabilization that gets reconciled at the annual true-up. Can your legal/finance suggest specific language that limits ACME's short-term upside risk?

I can take a call tomorrow at 11am PT if you confirm.

—Ellen
Senior Procurement Manager, Acme Corp

Internal — forwarding ACME redline and request. High level: ACME legal wants a monthly hard floor. That conflicts with our standard annual true-up.

Proposed compromise (quick brainstorm):
- Keep annual true-up as the primary reconciliation; that preserves predictable revenue recognition for us and seasonality smoothing for them.
- Add a "monthly stabilization" adjustment: if ACME usage in a month falls below the agreed monthly soft-floor, Redwood issues a temporary stabilization credit for that shortfall; credits are noted but are only applied at annual true-up and limited in aggregate to X% of committed annual fees (cap to be determined by finance).
- Offer per-SKU floors only for the three enterprise SKUs ACME highlighted (SaaS-Core, Data-Stream, Embed-XL). For the rest, floor remains aggregate.

Marcus — can you run a sensitivity model showing (i) revenue exposure if we accept the hybrid, (ii) cap levels (5%, 10%, 15% of committed annual) and the impact on ARR/recognition? Need this by EOD tomorrow to present to legal.

Marissa — can you draft redline language that preserves annualization but adds the stabilization credit and the aggregate cap? Keep it short — ACME legal wants concrete wording. If you think finance/legal will still reject, flag for escalation to VP Sales.

I'll hold the call slot at 11am PT — please confirm availability.

Thanks,
Karthik

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Sounds reasonable — I will draft proposed amendment language that:
1) Keeps annual true-up as the default reconciliation.
2) Defines a "Monthly Stabilization Adjustment" equal to max(0, Monthly_Soft_Floor - Actual_Monthly_Usage) which will be tracked as a credit.
3) States that stabilization credits are applied at annual true-up and are capped at 10% of the committed annual fees unless otherwise agreed in writing.
4) Includes optional per-SKU floor language limited to the three named enterprise SKUs.

Marcus — please push your model by EOD tomorrow. Karthik — I can send the redline amendment as a tracked-change Word doc (Proposed_Amendment_v1.docx) before the call. If ACME won't accept a cap at 10%, propose we prepare a fallback with a 5% cap and a finance justification.

Marissa
